::: {.home-intro}
::: {.home-intro-copy}
I serve as Assistant Secretary in the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, under the
Office of the President of the Philippines. I provide evidence-based analysis
of selected policy and implementation issues that may warrant the Cabinet
Secretary’s attention, drawing on quantitative methods, agency inputs, and
field validation to prepare advice and options.

I hold a BSc in Mathematics with First Class Honours from the [University of
Bristol](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/2027/maths/bsc-mathematics/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} and am pursuing an MSc in Applied and
Computational Mathematics at [The Johns Hopkins University
(JHU)](https://ep.jhu.edu/programs/applied-and-computational-mathematics/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
My studies focus on statistical and causal inference, network science, game
theory, and the mathematical foundations of machine learning, with applied work
in social media analytics and an introduction to generative AI.
:::

## Teaching

I teach part-time at [Bulacan State
University](https://bulsu.edu.ph/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}. Next semester,
I will teach
[*Discrete Mathematics*](teaching/bulsu/discrete-mathematics/index.qmd) at the
[Bustos](https://bulsu.edu.ph/academics/campus/Bustos){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
Campus. I currently teach
[*Mathematics in the Modern World*](teaching/bulsu/math-modern-world/index.qmd)
and [*Living in the IT Era*](teaching/bulsu/living-it-era/index.qmd) at the
[San Rafael](https://bulsu.edu.ph/academics/campus/San%20Rafael){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
Campus. My [teaching materials](teaching/index.qmd) include original lecture
notes, exercises, and supplementary resources developed primarily for biology
students.

## Writing

I write [*Calculated*](calculated/index.qmd), a weekly Saturday column for the
*Manila Bulletin*. The newspaper's [author
archive](https://mb.com.ph/author/rj-nieto){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
provides links to the published essays.

## Hobby

My hobby is [independent mathematics, artificial intelligence, and
machine-learning research](research/index.qmd). My current project asks how
image-analysis methods respond when images are rotated, resized, poorly
exposed, or degraded by sensor noise, and whether those response patterns can
help identify acquisition problems. The work continues my University of Bristol dissertation,
*Computational Stability of Cubical Homology*; the
[thesis](https://github.com/reyjosephnieto/ph/blob/main/Nieto_TDA_Public_20260430.pdf){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
and [Python implementation](https://github.com/reyjosephnieto/ph){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
are publicly available.

## Earlier work

My earlier work spans technical writing, journalism, national broadcasting,
public affairs, government communications, and programme delivery. Further
details are available in my [CV](cv/index.qmd) and on
[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rjosephnieto/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
